submitted.rationale: Index 5 (Cu0.66Sb0.34) had the highest EQE of the three measured: 0.0147%, against 0.0047% at index 2 and 0.0037% at index 16. Its XRD shows a Cu-rich Cu-Sb-O phase that no listed MP structure matches well (best similarity 0.38). CuSb2O6, which MACE puts on the hull, is identified at index 16 and gave about 4x lower EQE.

rejected.reason: Nearly phase-pure CuSb2O6 (XRD similarity 0.84); measured EQE 0.0037%, about 4x below index 5.
Measured EQE 0.0047%, lower than index 5; it lies next to the more Cu-rich region, whose phase set differs from index 5's.
Not measured. XRD shows mostly CuSb2O6 with some of index 5's phase, so its EQE is expected to fall between the two.

consultations.verdict: Support, weakly: MEGNet puts Cu2SbO5, the closest Cu-rich ternary, at a 2.09 eV HSE gap, just below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it would absorb. MACE places that structure far above the hull (1.16 eV/atom), so the phase actually present is probably a different Cu-rich ternary. XRD agrees: index 5 matches none of the listed phases well. The CuSb2O6 gap of 0.02 eV is an unreliable prediction.

Support: MACE puts CuSb2O6 (mp-1188790) on the hull at 0 eV/atom with a strongly negative formation energy, so it should form cleanly. XRD at index 16 matches it with 0.84 similarity. MEGNet's 0.02 eV gap looks like a failure on a correlated Cu(II) oxide: CuSb2O6 is known experimentally to have a gap around 1.5-2 eV and to be photoanodically active. That is below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it would absorb.

Uninformative: MEGNet gives CuO a 0.015 eV gap, the same Cu(II) failure seen for CuSb2O6, so it cannot rank the Cu-rich end. I'm relying on the measurements instead. The Cu-rich unknown phase (index 5) gave 4x the EQE of CuSb2O6 (index 16). Index 2 sits at the boundary between index 5's phase and the different phase set seen at index 1, and the GP ranks it as the top UCB candidate.
